examples.en: I trimmed the fine hair on my face with a razor.

examples.ko: 복숭아 껍질에는 잔털이 많이 나 있어요.
examples.en: Peach skin has a lot of fine fuzz on it.

examples.ko: 제 얼굴의 잔털은 햇빛에 금색으로 보여요.
examples.en: The fine hair on my face looks golden in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 아기는 이마와 볼에 잔털도 나 있어요.
examples.en: The baby has fine hair on the forehead and cheeks too.

examples.ko: 잔털 제거 크림을 써 봤는데 피부가 따가웠어요.
examples.en: I tried a hair removal cream, but my skin stung.
It was so scary that even the fine hairs on my neck stood up.

explain: '솜털'과 비슷하지만, '잔털'은 얼굴, 팔, 다리에 난 가늘고 짧은 털을 말할 때 폭넓게 써요. 굵고 진한 털은 그냥 '털'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Fine hair grew on my arms, so I shaved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이나 얼굴에 가는 털이 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fine hair shows up on the body or face.

phrases.en: This fruit has a lot of fine hair on its skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 과일이나 식물에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for fruit and plants as well as people.
phrases.en_equiv: to have lots of fine hair

phrases.en: I removed the fine hair on my legs before summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미용 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about grooming and beauty.

explain_en: Fine, soft hair on the body or face. It is close to '솜털' (down), but 잔털 is used broadly for thin, short hairs on the face, arms and legs. Thick, dark hair is just called '털'.

examples.en: I sit cross-legged on the floor and eat.
If I sit cross-legged, my legs go numb.
The children sat in a circle with their legs crossed.
If sitting cross-legged is uncomfortable, sit on a chair.
I watched TV sitting cross-legged.

examples.ko: 명상할 때는 책상다리를 하고 허리를 펴요.
examples.en: When meditating, I sit cross-legged and straighten my back.

explain: 바닥에 앉아 두 다리를 꼬아 앞으로 모으는 자세예요. 보통 '책상다리를 하다'로 쓰고 '양반다리'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I sat on the floor cross-legged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 자세를 취한다는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic expression for taking this posture.

phrases.en: Grandfather always sits cross-legged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책상다리와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another word with the same meaning.

phrases.en: I learned the cross-legged pose in yoga class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동이나 명상에서 자세 이름으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when naming the posture in exercise or meditation.

explain_en: It is the sitting posture on the floor with your legs crossed in front of you. It is usually used as '책상다리를 하다', and people also call it '양반다리'.

examples.en: Her nose bridge is high, so her profile is pretty.
My nose bridge is low, so my glasses keep sliding down.
Wrinkles form on the bridge of my nose when I laugh.
I pushed my glasses up the bridge of my nose.

examples.ko: 새 마스크가 콧대를 꽉 눌러서 아파요.
examples.en: The new mask presses hard on my nose bridge and it hurts.
I made my nose bridge look higher with makeup.

explain: 코의 위쪽 길게 이어진 선에 써요. 콧구멍이나 코끝은 다른 말이에요. 안경, 마스크, 화장 이야기에 자주 나와요. 비유로도 쓰는 말이라서 아래 표현을 같이 보세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 인기가 많아서 콧대가 높아요.
phrases.en: be stuck-up; look down on others
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘난 척하고 다른 사람을 얕보는 태도를 말해요. 반대로 '콧대를 꺾다'는 잘난 척하는 사람의 기를 눌러 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a proud attitude of looking down on others. '콧대를 꺾다' means to take a boastful person down a peg.
phrases.en_equiv: have one's nose in the air

explain_en: It refers to the long upper line of the nose; the nostrils and the tip are different words. It comes up in talk about glasses, masks, and makeup. It is also used figuratively, so see the expression below.

t90.ax: I pushed my glasses up the bridge of my nose.

en: to be tangled; to be entangled; to be disheveled

examples.en: My hair got all messed up because of the wind.
My hair is always messy when I wake up.
The thread is so tangled that I can't undo it.

examples.ko: 헝클어진 머리로 학교에 갈 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't go to school with messy hair.

examples.ko: 방 안이 헝클어져 있어서 정리해야 해요.
examples.en: The room is a mess, so I need to tidy it up.

examples.ko: 서류가 헝클어지지 않게 파일에 꽂아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put the documents in a file so they don't get jumbled.

explain: 머리카락, 실, 끈처럼 길고 가는 것이 엉킬 때 가장 잘 어울려요. '흐트러지다'는 정돈된 것이 흩어질 때 쓰는 말이라 느낌이 조금 달라요. 사람이 일부러 그렇게 만들 때는 '머리를 헝클다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I went to school with messy hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 모습을 설명할 때 '헝클어진'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'heongkeureojin' before a noun to describe its look.

phrases.example: 목걸이 줄이 헝클어져서 풀 수가 없어요.
phrases.en: The necklace chain is tangled and I can't undo it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락뿐 아니라 실, 줄, 끈에도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works naturally for thread, cord, and string, not just hair.
phrases.en_equiv: for a cord to get tangled

phrases.en: I wore a hat so my hair wouldn't get messy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 활용으로 막고 싶은 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used to say what you want to prevent.

explain_en: It fits best for long, thin things like hair, thread, or string that get tangled. '흐트러지다' is for something neat that scatters, so the feel is a little different. When a person does it on purpose, use the active verb, as in '머리를 헝클다'.

examples.ko: 길에서 차가 고장 나서 견인차를 불렀어요.
examples.en: My car broke down on the road, so I called a tow truck.

examples.ko: 견인차가 우리 차를 정비소로 끌고 갔어요.
examples.en: The tow truck pulled our car to the repair shop.
I parked illegally and my car was towed.
They say the tow truck driver will arrive soon.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에 견인차 두 대가 왔어요.
examples.en: Two tow trucks came to the scene of the accident.
The towing cost was more expensive than I thought, which surprised me.

explain: 견인차는 고장 난 차나 불법 주차한 차를 끌고 가는 차예요. 보험을 쓰면 '긴급 출동'이라는 서비스로 부르기도 해요. 입말에서는 '레커차'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: A tow truck came and took the car away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입말에서 '견인차' 대신 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spoken word used in place of 견인차.

phrases.en: The tow truck came thirty minutes later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 요청한 뒤 차가 도착할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the truck arrives after you asked for help.

phrases.example: 불법 주차해서 제 차가 견인차에 끌려갔어요.
phrases.en: I parked illegally, so my car was towed away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 허락 없이 옮겨졌을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a car has been moved away without permission.

explain_en: A 견인차 tows away broken-down or illegally parked cars. With car insurance you can often call one as an '긴급 출동' (emergency dispatch) service. In casual speech it is also called '레커차'.

examples.en: If you cross the overpass, the subway station is right there.

examples.ko: 이 구름다리는 큰 도로 위에 있어요.
examples.en: This overpass is above a big road.
The night view from the overpass is wonderful.
I held my child's hand and crossed the overpass.
A new overpass was built between the parks.
The overpass stairs are high, so it's tiring.

explain: 도로나 철길 위로 사람이 걸어서 건너는 높은 다리예요. '육교'라고도 해요. 건물과 건물 사이를 잇는 다리를 말할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I cross the overpass and go to the bus stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 말이고, 도로 위를 건너는 다리는 일상에서 '육교'라고 더 많이 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning; for a bridge over a road, 육교 is the more common everyday word.

phrases.en: I looked down at the road from the overpass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다리 위에 있는 장소를 말할 때 '위'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 위 (on top) to talk about standing on the bridge.

phrases.en: The two buildings are connected by a bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물과 건물 사이를 잇는 다리를 말할 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a bridge linking two buildings.

explain_en: It is an elevated bridge people walk across over a road or railway, also called '육교'. It can also describe a bridge connecting two buildings.

en: at a good distance; far off

examples.en: The children just stood far off and watched.
I parked the car far away and walked.
I was scared of the dog, so I went around at a distance.

examples.ko: 멀찌감치 떨어져서 보면 그림이 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If you stand far back, you can see the painting better.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 나를 보고 멀찌감치 피해 갔어요.
examples.en: That person saw me and steered clear at a distance.
Drive keeping a good distance from the car ahead.

explain: 꽤 멀리 떨어져 있는 모양을 나타내요. 그냥 '멀리'보다 일부러 거리를 두거나 떨어져 있는 상황에 잘 어울려요. '멀찍이'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: I watched from a good distance away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀찌감치'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'meoljjigamchi', just a little shorter.

phrases.en: I was scared of the dog, so I moved far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 거리를 두고 물러날 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for deliberately keeping your distance.

phrases.en: I watch from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀찌감치'보다 일반적이고 일부러 거리를 두는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More general than 'meoljjigamchi', with less sense of keeping distance on purpose.

explain_en: It describes being quite far away. Compared with plain '멀리', it fits well when someone keeps their distance on purpose. '멀찍이' is used with the same meaning.

t90.ax: I parked the car far away and walked.

examples.en: The main road was blocked, so we went around by a side road.
Walking along the path through the forest is refreshing.

examples.ko: 지름길인 줄 알았는데 샛길이 막혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I thought it was a shortcut, but the side road was blocked.
Cars can't enter this side road.
The child was playing on a side path and got lost.

examples.ko: 논 사이의 샛길을 지나 건널목에 이르렀어요.
examples.en: We passed along a path between the rice fields and reached the crossing.

explain: 큰길에서 갈라져 나온 작은 길이에요. 빠르게 가는 '지름길'과는 달리, 단지 크기가 작은 길이라 돌아가거나 한적한 곳을 걸을 때 써요. 이야기나 행동이 본래 방향에서 벗어날 때 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: The story went off on a tangent and I forgot the main point.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 행동이 중심에서 벗어나 다른 쪽으로 흘러간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means that speech or behavior drifts away from the main point.

explain_en: Small shortcut path between main roads; spoken. It is a small path that branches off from a main road. Unlike '지름길' (a shortcut that is faster), it simply means a small road, so it is used for detours or quiet walks. It is also used figuratively when a story or action drifts away from the main direction.

examples.en: The captain sat in the cockpit and checked the plane.

examples.ko: 조종석 문은 비행 중에 잠겨 있어요.
examples.en: The cockpit door stays locked during the flight.

examples.ko: 아이는 장난감 비행기의 조종석을 신기하게 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The child gazed in wonder at the cockpit of the toy plane.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 실제 전투기 조종석에 앉아 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At the museum, you can sit in the cockpit of a real fighter jet.
What does the sky look like from the cockpit?
A helicopter cockpit is narrower than you'd think.

explain: '조종석'은 비행기, 헬리콥터, 우주선처럼 조종하는 사람이 앉는 자리예요. 자동차, 버스, 택시는 '운전석'이라고 하니까 '조종'과 '운전'을 구분해 보세요. 배는 '조타실'이라는 말을 써요.

phrases.example: 아이가 조종석에 앉아 보고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: The child wants to sit in the cockpit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리에 앉는다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for sitting in the seat.

phrases.en: I could see clouds through the cockpit window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조종석 안이나 주변에 있는 것을 말할 때 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before a noun to talk about things in or around the cockpit.

phrases.en: A helicopter cockpit is very narrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 탈것인지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the type of vehicle in front.

explain_en: The seat where the pilot or operator sits. 조종석 is the seat where the pilot sits in a plane, helicopter, or spaceship. For cars, buses, and taxis, Koreans say 운전석 instead, so keep 조종 and 운전 apart. For a ship's wheelhouse, the word is 조타실.

t90.ax: What does the sky look like from the cockpit?

examples.en: A new paved road has been built to the village.
Even when it rains, paved roads are easy to walk on.
We went through the mountain path and came out onto a paved road.
From where the paved road ends, it's a dirt road.

examples.ko: 이 길은 포장도로라서 자전거 타기 좋아요.
examples.en: This is a paved road, so it's good for cycling.
In winter the paved road froze and was slippery.

explain: 아스팔트나 시멘트로 단단하게 깔아 놓은 길이에요. 반대는 흙길이나 '비포장도로'예요. '비포장도로'는 차가 흔들려서 운전이 힘들다고 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 새 포장도로를 달리니까 차가 안 흔들려요.
phrases.en: The car doesn't shake on the new paved road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 달리는 길을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the road a car drives on.
phrases.en_equiv: to drive on a paved road

phrases.en: The dirt road became a paved road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 달라진 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a road that has been changed.

phrases.en: It's a paved path, so it's good for cycling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '포장된 길'이라고도 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple everyday way to say the same thing.

explain_en: It is a road laid firmly with asphalt or cement. The opposite is a dirt road, or '비포장도로'. '비포장도로' often comes up when saying the car shakes and driving is hard.

examples.en: I want to build a mud house in the countryside and live there.
That mud house was quite cool even in summer.

examples.ko: 산골에 있는 작은 흙집에서 하룻밤 잤어요.
examples.en: I stayed one night in a small mud house in the mountains.
I went to a mud-house experience village with the kids.

examples.ko: 마을 끝에 낡은 흙집이 한 채 남아 있어요.
examples.en: One old mud house remains at the end of the village.
It's a café with a cozy feel like a mud house.

explain: 흙으로 지은 집을 말해요. 황토로 지은 집은 '황토집'이라고도 하는데, 건강과 자연 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 지붕 재료로 이름 붙인 '초가집'과는 기준이 달라요.

phrases.en: A yellow-clay house is warm in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 황토로 지은 흙집을 말하고, 건강한 집이라는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A mud house made of yellow clay, with a healthy-living feel.

phrases.en: My friend built a mud house by himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 만든다고 할 때 '짓다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '짓다' when saying someone builds a house.

phrases.en: My grandfather lived in a mud house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사는 곳을 말할 때 조사 '에서'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the particle '에서' when talking about where someone lives.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a mud house

explain_en: House built of earth, rural and traditional (시골 흙집) It means a house built of earth. A house built of ocher clay is also called '황토집', which often comes up in talk about health and nature. It differs from '초가집', which is named for its thatched roof.

examples.en: I put a hook on the wall and hung my bag on it.
The captain is a pirate with a hook for one hand.
The string is caught on the hook and won't come loose.
At the butcher's, meat is hanging from hooks.

examples.ko: 갈고리 모양 손잡이가 달린 지팡이를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a cane with a hook-shaped handle.
The cat's claws are sharp like hooks.

explain: '걸이'나 '고리'는 걸어 두는 물건 전체에 쓰고, '갈고리'는 끝이 굽은 모양을 강조해요. 그래서 물건을 낚거나 매달 때 쓰는 날카로운 쇠붙이에 어울려요. '손'이나 '발톱' 모양을 말할 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I hung the towel on the hook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굽은 끝에 물건을 매달 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hanging something on a bent end.

phrases.en: I bent my finger into a hook shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝이 굽은 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a bent-end shape.

phrases.en: I put a ring on the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갈고리'보다 걸어 두는 물건 전체에 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 갈고리 for anything used to hang things.

explain_en: 걸이 and 고리 are general words for things that hold other things, while 갈고리 stresses a bent, pointed end. It suits a sharp metal piece used to catch or hang things. It is also often used to describe the shape of hands or claws.

examples.en: I bought a drill to make a hole in the wall.

examples.ko: 드릴 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The drill noise was so loud that I was startled.
The neighbors are working with a drill.

examples.ko: 전동 드릴은 나사를 박을 때도 편해요.
examples.en: An electric drill is also handy for driving in screws.
My father showed me how to use a drill.

examples.ko: 드릴을 쓸 때는 보안경을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear safety glasses when using a drill.

explain: 벽이나 나무에 구멍을 뚫는 공구예요. 전기로 돌리는 것은 '전동 드릴'이라고 해요. 영어 drill에는 '반복 훈련'이라는 뜻도 있지만 한국어 드릴은 보통 공구를 가리켜요.

phrases.en: I drilled a hole in the wall with an electric drill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전기로 돌리는 드릴을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a drill powered by electricity.

phrases.en: I drill a hole in the wood with a drill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드릴의 쓰임을 보여 주는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing that shows what a drill is used for.
phrases.en_equiv: drill a hole with a drill

phrases.en: The drill noise from next door is too loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사나 수리할 때 나는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the sound made during construction or repairs.

explain_en: This is the tool for boring holes in walls or wood; the electric kind is called 전동 드릴. English drill also means repeated practice, but in Korean 드릴 usually points to the tool.

examples.en: Please close the bottle cap tightly.
When I pulled the bathtub plug, the water drained.
The cap wouldn't open, so I popped it with a spoon.

examples.ko: 샴푸 마개를 열고 한 번 눌렀어요.
examples.en: I opened the shampoo cap and pressed once.
I sealed the bottle with a cork stopper.
There was no stopper, so all the water spilled.

explain: '뚜껑'은 위에서 덮는 것이고, '마개'는 구멍에 끼워 막는 것이에요. 그래서 '병마개'라고 하지만 냄비에는 '냄비 뚜껑'이라고 해요. '마개를 따다/열다/막다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The bottle cap won't open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 입구를 막는 마개를 붙여서 한 단어로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single compound word for the stopper of a bottle.

phrases.en: I opened the cola cap and drank it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 캔을 처음 열 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when opening a bottle or can for the first time.

phrases.en: When I pulled the sink plug, the water drained.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끼워져 있는 마개를 뽑는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to pull out a stopper that is inserted.

explain_en: A '뚜껑' covers from the top, while a '마개' is pushed into an opening to block it. So it is '병마개', but for a pot it is '냄비 뚜껑'. You say '마개를 따다/열다/막다'.
